why.vibe: Reviewers call the shared floor open and clean, but it is an office lounge rather than a room you would seek out.
why.uniq: An owner who holds the whole building, introduces members to each other and tweaks the place himself is rarer than the chain floors nearby.

why.work: Wi-Fi, outlets and app-key entry with no stated limit, but drop-in hours are not the 24-hour ones advertised.

entries.pitch: Owner-run share office a few minutes from Ueno; drop-in desks by the half hour in a bright lounge, with private offices and a members' community upstairs.
entries.best: Reviews describe the open lounge as the place for spreading out; the quiet low-price study area suits exam-style work. The 24-hour listing applies to office tenants, so treat drop-in as daytime.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets stated; reviewers call the connection good. Online registration issues an app key for the auto-locked door, and day-use check-in worked without staff. Meeting rooms are shared with the sister building 15 seconds away.
entries.headsUp: Google lists the 2nd building, and the 24-hour access is for rental-office contracts only, not drop-in. Owner openly says it is not aiming to be the cheapest.

quotes.text: お値打ちです。
オンライン上で登録からキーの発行、入室、利用までスムーズでした。
ネット環境は良好。いい感じです。
低価格で静かに作業ができるスペースや固定席のメニューもあります。

entries.summaryEn: A small set of very positive reviews, mostly from private-office tenants, praising the hands-on owner, the location and smooth app-based entry; the only caveat is that it is not the cheapest option and the perks favour members.

signals.crowding: quiet, member-heavy

entries.pitch: Big 90-seat coworking floor run by web agency LIG in a back street south of Ueno; cheap by the half hour with free drinks, but run rather loosely.
order: Free drink bar and water server (sometimes empty)
Microwave available for your own food
entries.best: Reviewers who go regularly describe it as quiet and clean; avoid sitting near the open-space groups if you have a call, and give yourself ten extra minutes for the QR entry on a first visit.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi, outlets, lockers, copier and bookable private booths; QR-code self check-in and check-out. Remote calls happen in the open space, so it is not a silent room. One source says drop-in is 10:00-19:00 only, another says 24-hour access.
entries.headsUp: Entrance is hard to find and the 2F booths are unsigned; reviewers report the posted Wi-Fi password being wrong and staff being hard to identify. The 24-hour and 10-19 claims conflict, so check before an evening visit.

quotes.text: 入口が分かりにくい以外は、静かな環境でした。
Wi-Fiのパスワードが違っていたり、自由に使える電子レンジが足元にあったりと運営は大雑把です。
綺麗ですし集中もできますが、たまにウォーターサーバーの水が切れていたり、チェックアウト用のQRがなかったりします。

entries.summaryEn: Regulars find it clean, quiet and cheap; complaints centre on the confusing entrance and QR check-in, loud video calls in the open space bleeding into booth meetings, and small operational lapses such as wrong Wi-Fi passwords and an empty water server.

signals.crowding: mixed; noisy groups at times

why.vibe: A clean but slightly worn karaoke room with a big screen is comfortable rather than lovely.
why.uniq: A private karaoke room with a drink bar as your office is a genuinely different idea in a district of office floors.
why.food: Drink bar plus a full karaoke kitchen menu, from lunch sets to the famous honey toast.
why.work: Private, calls unrestricted and a fair day cap; loses a point for the 20:00 finish and the crowded reception.

entries.pitch: Karaoke chain Pasela rents its private rooms as daytime work booths on the 4F opposite Ueno Park; a room of your own for calls, drink bar included.
order: Drink bar included with the coworking plan
Karaoke menu to order: honey toast, lunch sets
entries.best: Weekday daytime, when the rooms are otherwise empty; coworking runs 9:30-20:00 while the karaoke floor goes on to 05:00. Reception gets busy from around 20:00, so arrive early or book.
entries.workNotes: Private room with Wi-Fi and a copier; you can talk, take calls and run meetings freely. Two-hour minimum, then priced by block up to a ¥4,200 daily cap. No outlets stated in the claims, though karaoke rooms generally have one.
entries.headsUp: The Google listing and reviews are for the karaoke venue, not the work plan. Soundproofing is described as ordinary, so a loud neighbour can be heard; the facilities are a little dated but kept clean.

quotes.text: 私が使った部屋は隣室の音が少し気になりましたが、部屋の防音性能は通常レベルなので
ファシリティは少〜し古くなってきましたが、清潔に保たれています。
この時間帯は受付付近がかなり混雑しています。

entries.summaryEn: Reviews cover the karaoke business: polite staff, generous honey toast and lunch deals, family-friendly rooms, with grumbles about average sound quality, an outdated song app and evening queues at reception. None mention the coworking plan.

signals.crowding: reception busy after 20:00

why.vibe: Reviewers praise the interior, the chair comfort and the calm, with a cinema next door.
why.uniq: A café, a paid lounge and a screening room under one roof is a distinct model that the group repeats in Jiyugaoka and Yoyogi-Uehara.

why.work: Everything a day desk needs, but weekend crowds and the café-side hour limit keep it off full marks.

entries.pitch: Café-plus-lounge from the (tefu) group by Shimokitazawa station: barista café downstairs, two-storey work lounge with unlimited drinks and call booths.
order: Lounge: unlimited barista drinks and snacks on the plan
Café counter: latte, grilled cheese, evening mains around ¥1,600 with a drink
entries.best: Weekday mornings just after the 09:00 opening, when the café is empty while the station Starbucks is packed; the window sofa seats have outlets. Saturdays are crowded and groups struggle for seats.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets throughout, video-call booths in the lounge, no time limit on the day plan. The café side may impose a one-hour limit when busy; the lounge is priced by the hour or as a day pass.
entries.headsUp: One reviewer got a brusque response asking about lounge plans at reception; another waited 30 minutes for a sandwich. Café seating is not the same as the paid lounge, so check which you are paying for.

entries.pitch: Nomura's H1T satellite-office chain, 7F of an office block one minute from Nakameguro station; open desks and glass booths booked by the hour through Instabase.
order: Free Morinaga paper-pack drinks, yoghurt and pudding (often out of stock)
entries.best: One reviewer found it unexpectedly empty; another found the private booths nearly full on a weekday afternoon. Restocking was spotted on Tuesday and Wednesday after lunch. Open 08:30-20:00 daily.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets; wall-mounted monitors at eye level in the L booths, a sofa-type R booth, meeting rooms. Voices carry across the floor, so video calls from open seats are not advised. Booking runs through Instabase rather than walk-in.
entries.headsUp: The free drink shelf is frequently empty and the frosted booth glass is more see-through than it looks. Toilets are outside the space by the lift.

why.food: Free drinks and nothing else.
why.work: Cheap day cap, late hours, calls permitted and a quiet room; the unstaffed online sign-in and lounge noise are the friction.

entries.pitch: Cheap study-room-cum-lounge on the 3F of an old building three minutes south of Nakano station; a talking lounge and a silent room, open till 23:00.
order: No microwave, per a reviewer's request
entries.best: Late evenings are quiet and lightly used; drop-in reception closes at 23:00. Pick the silent room if you want to avoid the lounge, where loud remote interviews have been reported.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi, copier and lockers; the lounge allows calls and video meetings, the office room does not. Staff are absent at night, so you register and pay online before entry, re-entering your details each visit.
entries.headsUp: The building is old with narrow, steep stairs and a single unisex toilet; several reviewers found staff curt or unhelpful. Not the polished new-office room some expect.

quotes.text: 夜遅めだからか利用者は少なめで静かで快適です。

entries.summaryEn: Reviewers value the low price, late hours and the separation of talking and silent rooms; the recurring complaints are unfriendly or mumbling staff, an ageing building with steep stairs, a shared single toilet and the occasional very loud caller in the lounge.

quotes.text: オープンスペースは日本銀行を見渡せるので、良い景色を見ながら仕事が出来る

entries.headsUp: Closes at 18:00 and shuts entirely at weekends; seat count is low and video calls have been halted by staff.

quotes.text: 受付の方が大変親切です。安心して利用出来る環境です。

why.food: A free drink bar with a wider than usual coffee and tea selection, nothing to eat.
why.work: Long weekday hours, uncrowded, meeting rooms; closed at weekends.

entries.headsUp: Closed Saturday and Sunday; the day rate is the highest in this batch. Hours differ between sources, so confirm before a late finish.

quotes.text: 丸の内らしくモダンで落ち着いた感じのオフィスでした。
場所がそんなに混み合うこともなく、いつもゆったりと使わせていただいています。
ドリンクもコーヒーとお茶のバリエーションが比較的多いので落ち着いて仕事ができます。

entries.summaryEn: Only a handful of reviews, all positive: a calm, modern space that is seldom full, with a better drink selection than most. No complaints recorded.

why.uniq: Focus pods and a magazine library give it a little more character than the standard floor.
why.food: Unlimited free drinks, nothing solid.
why.work: Phone booths, meeting rooms, outlets and 12-hour weekdays; closed at weekends.

entries.pitch: Plus OURS by Expert Office, a tidy Tokyo Tatemono coworking floor four minutes from the Yaesu exit; suits a full weekday with calls to make.
entries.best: Weekdays 8:00 to 20:00, closed weekends. Reviewers found it uncrowded; the enclosed focus seats are the pick for concentration.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets stated; phone booths and meeting rooms (Steelcase chairs, per one review); magazine library. Day registration described as quick.
entries.headsUp: Weekdays only. Listed on Google under the Expert Office name, so search for that if the map draws a blank.

オフィス環境は綺麗で、ドリンクも飲み放題で快適でした。

entries.summaryEn: Few but consistently positive reviews: smooth day-pass registration, a clean room with good chairs and enclosed focus seats, free drinks, and plenty of space. No complaints recorded.

why.vibe: Bright and spacious, but reviewers describe a crowded floor with groups treating the talk zone as a lounge.
why.uniq: A standard WORK STYLING fit-out; the Midtown address is the draw.
why.food: Drink bar and snacks, comparable to other branches; no ice machine.
why.work: Per-minute billing, membership screening, gate friction and crowding all add up to real hassle.

entries.pitch: Mitsui Fudosan's flagship WORK STYLING on 7F of Tokyo Midtown Yaesu; a corporate members' floor that sells minutes, best for those already registered.
order: Free drink bar and snack corner
Fridge on the floor; no ice machine
entries.best: Weekdays 8:00 to 21:00, weekends 10:00 to 18:00. Reviewers report heavy afternoon crowds and private rooms booked out; go early and book a room ahead.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi, outlets and phone booths; private rooms bookable; a designated talk-OK zone allows calls. Entry is by QR code at the building gate, and Wi-Fi details are posted at the cafe corner, not in the rooms.
entries.headsUp: Membership is subject to a screening that one applicant says went unanswered for weeks; the QR gate and lift system confuse first-timers; allow 10 to 15 minutes from the platform.

quotes.text: 利用者も多いですがスペースもまぁまぁ広くて良かったです。
オフィスエリアの出入りに、ゲートでQRが必要で、知らないとアタフタして後ろの人に舌打ちされそうで焦る
直前だと空きがほとんどない。
だいたいエレベーターの待ちも含めて駅のホームから10分15分かかります。

entries.summaryEn: Staff are praised, but reviews split on the rest: crowding, noisy groups in the talk zone, confusing QR gates, private rooms hard to book, and one applicant left waiting indefinitely on the membership check.

signals.crowding: busy afternoons

why.vibe: Clean, well air-conditioned and calm despite the calls-OK policy, but a plain fourth-floor office room.
why.uniq: A well-run chain branch with nothing you would not find at the others.
why.food: Free drink bar only; bring-your-own food is allowed.
why.work: All-seat power, fast Wi-Fi, calls OK and 14-hour weekdays; the small floor is the one limit.

entries.pitch: Basis Point's busiest branch, one minute from Ikebukuro east exit: walk-in coworking with outlets at every seat, free drinks and calls allowed.
order: Bring your own food; eating at desks allowed
entries.best: Weekdays 8:00 to 22:00, weekends from 10:00. Around 20 open seats, so mornings are the safer bet; the new private booths are the spot for a sensitive call.
entries.workNotes: Outlets at every seat, Wi-Fi reviewers call fast, conversation, calls and web meetings all permitted on the floor. First visit needs a free registration but no ID or booking; private booths and a 1 to 4 person BOX (¥1,980/h) are bookable, laptops rentable at ¥1,100/day.
entries.headsUp: Small floor of roughly 20 seats that can feel cramped; chairs sit low and one reviewer found the clientele scruffy. Closed over New Year.

quotes.text: 雰囲気や設備もよく、作業に集中できました
会話・通話OKでも周りに配慮されてる方が多く、話し声等あまり気にならず作業に集中できました
席数が20席程度、少し狭さを感じたのでフロアスペースがもう少し広いとありがたいと感じました。
椅子がかなり低い。

entries.summaryEn: Nearly 500 reviews averaging 4.3: fast Wi-Fi, outlets everywhere, free drinks, clean toilets and courteous staff, with calls tolerated without much noise. Complaints are the tight 20-seat floor, low chairs and awkward drink dispensers.

signals.crowding: small floor, about 20 seats

why.vibe: Clean and well kept with decent wheeled chairs, but a plain room with music on and the occasional boor.
why.uniq: The snack-and-peripherals-included model at this price is its own idea.
why.food: Free drinks and a small snack selection; nothing prepared.
why.work: Outlets, lockers, printing and a free meeting booth over long hours; noise and a semi-open booth hold it back.

entries.pitch: Independent coworking room on 3F above a Lawson, seven minutes east of Ikebukuro; cheap day rate with free drinks, snacks and printing.
order: Free drink bar (coffee machine, no milk drinks)
Bring your own food; eat at any seat
entries.best: Weekdays 9:00 to 22:00, weekends shorter; app booking means you will not be turned away full. Background music plays, so it is not for silence-seekers.

entries.headsUp: Reception is separated from the work floor, so loud callers and rough manners go unpoliced; the only way in is the lift. Hours differ between the sheet and Google.

quotes.text: そこら中に転がったコンセントハブもありがたい。
完全個室ではないけどWEB会議等をして良いブースが、予約すれば追加料金なしで使えたり
音楽がかかっているので、本当に静かな場所で集中したい方には向かないかもです。
受付とワーキングスペースは完全に別れているので店員さんも気づきにくく注意もできない状況です。

entries.summaryEn: Praised for value, kind staff, free drinks and snacks, lent-out peripherals and outlets everywhere; criticised for background music, loud all-day callers, and a layout that keeps staff out of earshot of bad behaviour.

why.food: Drinks plus bread and snacks, with an alcohol option, is more than a drink bar.
why.work: Long daily hours, but slow afternoon Wi-Fi, fiddly check-in and high prices count against a working day.

order: Free drink bar (coffee, cafe au lait, soft drinks)
entries.best: Open 8:00 to 22:00 daily. Weekend mornings are quiet; by afternoon the Wi-Fi bogs down and the coffee runs out. Take a terrace seat or a booth for a meeting.
entries.workNotes: Outlets and Wi-Fi standard for the chain, booth seating for meetings, books on shelves. Reviewers say weekends need a booking and that check-in is fiddly; Wi-Fi was too slow for a client call in two reviews.
entries.headsUp: The dearest hourly rate in this batch; Wi-Fi slows when full, vocal music plays, and seat-hogging goes unmanaged. No bookshop attached, unlike other branches.

quotes.text: 午後は人が増えたからかWi-Fiが遅くなり作業はできる状態じゃなかった
テラス席もあったりで席数多めのゆったりとした作り。
土日は予約しないと席がないときがある。
Wifiが遅くて、商談は危ない。

entries.summaryEn: Mixed at 3.9: the terrace, seat count and snack selection are liked, but reviewers report Wi-Fi collapsing on busy afternoons, drinks running out, loud callers, people hogging two seats, and a laborious check-in.

signals.crowding: weekends need booking

why.uniq: A standard nex private-office floor.
why.food: Free tea, coffee and sports drinks.
why.work: Small drop-in allowance, a fussy app, poor reception for calls and stair-only access.

entries.pitch: THE HUB's basement branch opposite Seibu, a minute from the station; a members-first private-office floor that sells drop-in slots through its app.
order: Free drink bar (tea, coffee, sports drinks)
entries.best: Sources disagree: 24 hours per Google and the chain, 7:00 to 21:00 per another listing; reception is weekdays only. Only 16 open seats, so weekday daytime with a booking is the safe play.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi, meeting rooms, printer; chat-OK and silent zones plus private rooms. Drop-in is booked through the nex app, which reviewers describe as buggy and inflexible; phone signal is poor in the basement.
entries.headsUp: Basement entry via stairs only (the lift is closed), musty air, a room that runs cold in winter, and a ¥ rise in 2026. One drop-in visitor could not find the toilet.

quotes.text: 地下なのでかび臭さも気になり、快適さはあまり感じませんでした。
池袋は地下なので電波が少し悪いので電話がしにくいです！あとは基本寒いです！
エレベータはあるものの閉鎖されており、入退店は階段のみです。
値上げしたようです。

entries.summaryEn: A 3.4 average: the clean, office-like interior and station proximity are liked, but reviewers complain of a musty, cold basement, weak phone signal, a buggy booking app that refuses changes, and stairs-only access.

signals.crowding: 16 drop-in seats

why.vibe: Reviewers describe a clean, stylish, very quiet room with window light and wide desks.
why.uniq: A shoes-off coworking floor with a community feel is rare in Ikebukuro.
why.food: A water server and nothing else.
why.work: Good Wi-Fi and booths, but drop-in is capped at weekday 10 to 18 with no weekend access.

entries.pitch: Shoes-off co-ba on 4F by the Metro 1A exit; a calm, well-lit members' room that sells a weekday day pass to walk-ins.
order: Water server only; bring your own coffee
entries.best: Drop-in is weekdays 10:00 to 18:00 only (every other Monday until 17:00). Reviewers never found it full; the window seats get natural light and the half-booths suit web meetings.
entries.workNotes: Fast Wi-Fi, printer, wide desks, semi-private booths; web meetings are fine. No hourly drop-in per the sheet, though a 2024 review mentions ¥660 per hour via the ii Office app outside staffed hours. No reservation or membership needed for the day pass; shoes come off at the door.
entries.headsUp: No weekend or holiday drop-in and no private rooms; the building lift is old and grubby. Google's 7:00 to 22:00 hours are for members.

quotes.text: 平日も休日も利用しましたが、満席で座れないということはありませんでした。
特に窓側の席や会議室は、静かで集中しやすく、パソコン作業やWeb会議に最適です。
良きと思いますが、静か過ぎます。
ドリンクはウォーターサーバーあり。

entries.summaryEn: Only seven reviews but a 4.6 average: quiet, clean, never full, helpful staff, good window seats and booths for calls. Minor gripes are an old lift, hourly rather than half-hourly billing on the app, and a room some find too silent.

signals.crowding: never full

why.vibe: Clean and well equipped, but a self-service office suite with corridor chatter.
why.uniq: A standard ii Office franchise floor.
why.food: No drink service is mentioned anywhere.
why.work: Booths help, but doorless booths, unstaffed disputes, lock trouble and fixed air-con are real friction.

entries.pitch: Unstaffed ii Office franchise on 3F three minutes from the east exit; app-unlocked desks and semi-private booths for people who can cope without a front desk.
entries.best: The sheet says Mon to Sat 10:00 to 19:00, Google says 24 hours (app members). Booths are the reason to come; book one for a call and expect to hear the neighbours.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets stated; bookable semi-private booths with monitors, though booths have no doors and one monitor's audio failed. Entry is by app-unlocked door, which several reviewers struggled with.
entries.headsUp: No staff on site: one visitor found a stranger in their booked booth and was told to sort it out themselves, with no refund. Air-con cannot be adjusted and the room ran hot in summer.

quotes.text: 半個室はドアがないので他の方の声が丸聞こえ、オンラインに入ってきてやりづらかったです。
スタッフは常駐していないため，何かあったときの対応は自力解決になり
エアコンの温度設定が個室でも変えられず、暑すぎました。
入り口の鍵が開かなかった。

entries.summaryEn: Cleanliness is praised, but recent reviews are rough: doorless booths that leak sound into calls, a locked entrance, unadjustable heat, and a double-booked booth with no staff to resolve it and no follow-up.

why.vibe: Clean and comfortable per reviews, but the room is a karaoke box with the lights up.
why.uniq: A karaoke box as a private office with room service is unlike anything else here.
why.food: Proper hot food to order and an hourly drink from a long menu.
why.work: A door, a monitor and calls whenever you like; weekday-only hours and a shifting timetable limit it.

entries.pitch: Pasela's daytime coworking at the west exit: a private karaoke box to yourself, hourly drinks and a food menu, for anyone who needs a door that shuts.
order: One free drink per hour from the karaoke menu
Full Pasela food menu orderable to the room
entries.best: Weekdays only; Google shows some days until past midnight and Fridays until 17:00, so check the week's timetable. Any room is private, so time of day matters less than availability.
entries.workNotes: Private rooms with large monitors, Wi-Fi, phone booths and a loan cupboard of cables and peripherals; 30 seats. Calls and meetings are unrestricted inside your own room. Also usable through OFFICEPASS.
entries.headsUp: Two sources give different tariffs (¥1,000 for 3 hours versus ¥600 an hour up to ¥4,200), so confirm at the desk; closed Saturday and Sunday and the closing hour varies by week.

quotes.text: カラオケ歌う必要ないから、フロアも静か
貸し出しアイテムも豊富で、1時間に1杯ドリンクが無料で豊富な種類から選べるのも良かったです。
個室でとても快適に滞在できます。

entries.summaryEn: A 4.6 average from 78 reviews: private rooms, good food, an hourly free drink and a generous loan kit; the only reservation is a lukewarm 'it was alright' and a wish for a monthly plan.

why.work: A private room with monitor and open calls, but weekday-only with a variable closing time.

why.uniq: The secretary service and altitude lift it above a plain floor.
why.food: A business coffee machine is part of the service; nothing else on site.
why.work: Good kit and meeting rooms, but unpublished drop-in terms and reception-hours access.

entries.pitch: Servcorp's serviced office on the 45th floor of Sunshine 60, with bilingual secretaries and city views; built for tenants, with casual desks a secondary line.
entries.best: Reception runs weekdays 8:30 to 17:30 (members have 24-hour access); a weekday morning with an appointment is the realistic way in. Any seat has the 45F outlook.
entries.workNotes: Open floor allows web meetings; stationery and a multifunction printer on hand; meeting rooms for 1 to 3 people bookable from 10 minutes. Drop-in pricing is not published on the sheet, so expect to enquire.
entries.headsUp: Closed at weekends for non-members; reviews are almost all from office tenants, so the casual-desk experience is undocumented. Use the Higashi-Ikebukuro exit 7 link rather than walking from Ikebukuro.

quotes.text: 一般的なワーキングスペースは席の間隔が狭いところが多いのですが、ここは違いますよ♪
文房具・複合機が備え付けられているので、PCさえあれば手ぶらで行けます。
業務用コーヒーメーカーの利用もサービス内容に含まれている

entries.summaryEn: A 4.5 average built on tenant reviews: attentive, English-capable staff, clean and roomy desks, a stocked printer and coffee machine, and a convenient Sunshine City setting. No drop-in reviews and no complaints.

why.uniq: A conventional BIZcomfort floor; the balcony is the only flourish.
why.food: Free drinks in the cafe zone and an ice machine.
why.work: Zoned quiet and calls areas with staff on hand; drop-in hours end early and exclude weekends.

entries.pitch: BIZcomfort's three-floor Ikebukuro west branch with a concierge desk, zoned quiet and chat areas and a balcony; a no-fuss weekday drop-in.
order: Free drink bar in the cafe booth zone
entries.best: Drop-in runs weekdays 9:00 to 18:00 with last entry at 17:00; Google's 24-hour listing is for monthly members. Pick the silent booth zone to work or the cafe booth zone for calls.
entries.workNotes: No booking or registration for drop-in. Three zones: silent booths, work booths and a talk-OK cafe booth area where online meetings are fine. Reception is staffed on 6F; private rooms are available.
entries.headsUp: Drop-in ends at 17:00 entry and is closed at weekends and holidays. The 3.5 star average sits oddly against a run of five-star reviews posted the same month as an anniversary event.

quotes.text: フリースペース広いので仕事に集中できます。受付もあるので困った時の対応も早いです。

製氷機があるのが暑い夏場には嬉しいです。

entries.summaryEn: Recent reviews are uniformly positive about the concierge staff, cleanliness, quiet and the freedom to take online meetings; the 3.5 overall implies older complaints (one mentions past bad-mannered users) that are no longer visible.

why.vibe: Clean, well cleaned and comfortable chairs, but reviews describe a room that fails at its one job of being quiet.
why.uniq: The study-cafe format with classical music and a no-talk rule is a distinct idea.
why.food: A drink bar and nothing to eat.
why.work: No calls permitted, a card-key entry, and repeated noise complaints outweigh the long hours.

entries.pitch: Benkyo Cafe's Ikebukuro study lounge near Junkudo: a silent, drink-bar members' room that takes cashless visitors by the hour, aimed at exam candidates.
order: No food beyond drinks in the workspace
entries.best: Visitors weekdays 9:00 to 23:00, Saturday 10:00 to 22:00, Sunday 10:00 to 21:00 (the 6:00 opening is for members). Bring earplugs; the door-closed focus room still has music and slurping.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi, printer, meeting rooms, good office chairs and large monitors to borrow. Conversation and calls are banned in the workspace and eating is not allowed. Cashless payment only; entry is by physical card key rather than app.
entries.headsUp: Two sources disagree on the tariff (¥880/h and ¥3,300/day versus ¥500/h and ¥2,500/day). Several reviews accuse staff of chatting loudly with regulars and describe rude, noisy older users.

quotes.text: そして最大の問題点が入出管理にカードキーが必要なところ。
本気で勉強したい人には絶対お勧めしません。
店員さんが一番うるさいです。
勉強カフェさんはオフィスチェアが良いので重宝しています。

entries.summaryEn: A 3.5 average with a sharp split: the facilities, chairs, cleanliness and monitor loans are praised, but multiple reviewers say staff and regulars talk and laugh loudly, users slurp and chew, and the card-key system is dated.

why.food: No drink service is mentioned; reviewers point to shops nearby.
why.work: Long weekday hours, large desks, zoned calls and silence at a low price; Sunday closure and bleed-through noise hold it back.

entries.pitch: Entre Salon's big Ikebukuro branch, 83 desks in silent and talk zones five minutes from the station; a cheap all-day desk for sales staff and solo founders.
order: Convenience stores and restaurants on the street
entries.best: Weekdays 8:00 to 21:00, Saturday 9:00 to 18:00, Sunday closed. Rarely full per reviewers; the silent zone (36 seats) is the pick, since the free lounge next door fills and gets loud after lunch.
entries.workNotes: Two zones: 36 silent desks and 47 where chat and calls are allowed, plus 2 private rooms and meeting rooms from ¥400 per 30 minutes. Drop-in price is not on the sheet; one 2026 reviewer paid ¥1,100 for a 9:00 to 18:00 day, booked ahead. Re-entry allowed.
entries.headsUp: Monthly contracts carry a six-month lock-in that caught one reviewer out; some partitions are grubby and chair adjusters broken. Web-meeting users may pick up lounge noise through the door.

quotes.text: 1回1,100円と格安で9：00〜18：00の間利用でき、静かで仕事が捗った。
オープンスペースはそこまで広くはないですが満席になることはあまりなく、使いたい時に使えます。
昼過ぎはほぼ満席で結構な音量の声が聞こえてきました。Web会議をされている方は音が入りそうです。
最短2ヶ月契約のつもりが、6ヶ月ロックされて4万円くらい損失。

entries.summaryEn: A 4.2 average padded by networking-event attendees; genuine users praise the cheap day rate, big desks, quiet and good manners, while complaints cover a contract lock-in, dirty partitions, broken chairs and lounge noise reaching the work zone.

entries.best: Open 7:00 to 24:00 every day, so early mornings and late evenings are its edge. Take a proper chair rather than a bar stool; the terrace is for breaks.
entries.workNotes: Nearly every seat has power; two bookable phone booths; lockers and a meeting room; hotel shower available. Wi-Fi is contested: one reviewer calls it fast, another says it could not hold a Zoom call.
entries.headsUp: Reviews complain of cramped, knee-less bar seating, squeaky chairs, overbooking, rowdy guests, no drinks service at one visit and a check-out terminal failure. Drink claims conflict, so do not count on coffee.

チェックアウト時には端末異常があり待たされたりとオペレーションにも問題あり。
店員さんは感じよかったです。

entries.summaryEn: A 4.0 split between fans of the friendly staff, terrace, comfortable main seats and happy-hour beer, and detractors who found Wi-Fi unfit for calls, poor coffee, cramped stools, overbooking and having to wash their own cups.

立地もよくすごく綺麗で使いやすかったです。
コンビニ2つ越えて、バイク店の2階ですね。

why.vibe: Comfortable chairs and a surprising hush for Koen-dori, but dim lighting, creaky floors and an old public building drag it down.
why.uniq: Coworking inside a workers' welfare hall with a silent upper floor is an odd enough idea to stand out.
why.food: A ¥100 Doutor vending machine and no bins is as basic as it gets.
why.work: Outlets, decent Wi-Fi, a ¥1,980 day cap and a no-talking floor; the two-step check-in and noise leaks are the limitations.

entries.pitch: Budget coin-op coworking on two floors of the ageing Kinro Fukushi Kaikan on Koen-dori; a silent 2F for solo grind, a chattier 1F below.
order: Doutor coffee vending machine, ¥100 a cup
Bring your own food; no bins, so rubbish goes home with you
entries.best: The conversation-banned 2F on a weekday evening, when one reviewer counted two other people; 1F takes the talkers. Mondays close at 17:00.

entries.headsUp: It is a municipal welfare hall: creaking floors, school-style toilets, noise carrying between floors and passing ad trucks; one October 2024 review found the whole building shut on a day Google said open.

コーヒーの自動販売機があり1杯100円で飲める。
他の人が通ると床がミシミシ言う
時々巡回してくるアドトラックがうるさいけれども

why.uniq: A curated creative lounge with a library, exhibitions and a coffee-grinding ritual is not something the chains offer.
why.food: Proper drip coffee you make yourself plus a vending machine; real food is downstairs, not in the room.
why.work: Long hours, booths and lent monitors, but hourly-only pricing and a clunky sign-up limit it to short sessions.

entries.pitch: Beach-themed basement coworking by Shibuya's new south exit: wave soundtrack, free drinks, borrowable monitors and a sociable events crowd; day rate only.
entries.best: Full days, since there is no hourly rate. Check the current schedule first: Google now shows weekdays 10:00-21:00 and closed at weekends, and a mid-2026 review mentions a renovation period.
entries.workNotes: Open floor allows conversation, phone and web calls; soundproof TEL booths are free but booking-only; monitors and gadgets lent free; registration runs through LINE and one visitor found it slow. First visit is half price if you show the website.
entries.headsUp: Hours are in flux: the listing says 9-22 daily, Google says weekdays only, and the space may be mid-refit. Cool white lighting and the longer walk from the Hachiko side put some off.

quotes.text: 波のBGMがこんなにも心地良いなんて。
最新機器が利用し放題、ドリンクも飲み放題。
いまはリニューアル期間中？

entries.summaryEn: Strong 4.7 rating: clean, friendly staff who act on surveys, free gadgets and drinks, and a calm floor outside event hours; the few grumbles are day-only pricing, LINE sign-up, cool lighting and distance from the main exits.

signals.crowding: small and can be busy

entries.headsUp: No Google listing matched and there are no reviews; the listing does not confirm drop-in at all. Treat it as a rental-desk operation until told otherwise.
entries.summaryEn: No recent Google reviews to draw on.

why.work: Outlets everywhere, Wi-Fi, meeting rooms and 08-23 hours; the price makes a full day an expensive habit.

order: Unlimited snacks, soft drinks and alcohol included
Frozen meals (often sold out by mid-morning)

entries.workNotes: Outlets at every seat, stable Wi-Fi, bookable rooms suited to online meetings; online booking and tablet check-in with no lengthy registration; over 100 magazines free to read.
entries.headsUp: Sources disagree on the address (Scramble Square 11F versus Tsutaya 4F) and on price, which has risen; regulars complain the lounge shrank to one floor with thinner snack and frozen-food stock.

午前10時半に行ったら全部品切れで、食べられませんでした。

entries.pitch: Independent drop-in on 3F of an old building by Akihabara station; monitors on every table and long weekday hours, for travelling workers and small meetings.
entries.best: Weekdays 07:30-21:00 give the longest run; the morning and evening 3-hour deal at ¥1,100 is the value slot. Weekends 10:00-19:00.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets, external displays on tables, receipts issued, flexible extensions reported; used for both solo work and small group meetings and online streaming.
entries.headsUp: Building is old (rooms are clean); one late-2025 review says the meeting room advertised online is now an office, and another says service has slipped. Separate smoking area on site.

quotes.text: ビル自体古いですが、東京のコワーキングスペースの中でも、かなり使い勝手が良いです。
テーブルごとに外付けモニターが置いてあるところが良い。
ホームページに「会議室あり」とありますが、現在はオフィスになっており使用できませんでした。
駅近以外のメリットない。

entries.summaryEn: Reviews (4.4, 105) like the station proximity, per-table monitors, flexible staff and long weekday hours; the building is dated, the meeting room may no longer exist, and one reviewer feels service has declined.

why.vibe: Clean and pleasant per the one drop-in review; 3.6 overall.
why.uniq: A generic small-town shared office.
why.food: No drinks mentioned anywhere.
why.work: A 17:00 close, weekday-only opening, a joining fee and blocked VPN add up to real friction.

entries.pitch: Small rental office and coworking room five minutes south of Tachikawa station; weekday-only desks with a joining fee, for locals rather than visitors.
order: Bring your own light food (take rubbish away)
entries.best: Weekdays only, 10:00-17:00 per Google, so it is a daytime room; the 2024 reviewer found it clean and comfortable.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi, meeting room and multifunction printer; a 2019 review reports VPN connections blocked and no rubbish bins, so carry your waste out.
entries.headsUp: First visit costs an extra ¥1,320 registration. Closed weekends and finishes at 17:00. Several reviews concern the virtual-office post service rather than the desks.

quotes.text: ドロップインで利用しました。綺麗で使い勝手よく、居心地良かったです。
・ゴミ箱がありません。軽食は持ち込み可ですが、ゴミは自分で持ち帰る必要があります。
・VPNが制限されています。接続しようとしても繋がりません。

entries.summaryEn: Sparse reviews (3.6, 12): a recent drop-in found it clean with friendly staff; an older one warns of no bins and a blocked VPN; others only concern the mail-forwarding service.

entries.nameJa: coin space 立川髙島屋S.C.店

why.vibe: Clean and high-ceilinged with good partitions, but a 2.5 rating and a chilly, bin-less room.
why.uniq: A standard Coin Space floor that happens to sit in a department store.
why.food: No drinks at all; bring your own.
why.work: Long hours and outlets, but the repeatedly measured weak Wi-Fi makes online meetings unreliable.

entries.pitch: Coin Space partitioned study floor on 7F of Tachikawa Takashimaya; 07:00-23:00, cheap by the half hour, loved by exam students, not by anyone on Zoom.
entries.best: Mornings, before the Wi-Fi degrades; one regular recommends the F area for its high ceiling and partition height. Late evenings empty out, which a parent found unnerving.
entries.workNotes: Outlets at desks (some blocked by the desk-lamp plug), partitioned seats and semi-private rooms, meeting rooms, meetings permitted at seats; Wi-Fi measured at 20Mbps at best and under 2Mbps in the afternoon by several reviewers.
entries.headsUp: Do not rely on the Wi-Fi for calls; four separate reviews report Zoom dropping. No bins, no drinks, air-con runs cold. Monthly-plan billing is by emailed link and drew complaints.

quotes.text: 他の方も書いてますが、とにかく激弱wi-fiです。
午後以降、Wi-Fiの速度が極端に下がります。
ごみを捨てる場所がない。
天井が高く、パーティションの広さや高さ、照明の度合いや雰囲気、席の多さも気に入っていて、自習するのにとても良い場所です。

entries.summaryEn: Reviews (2.5, 29) split between students who value the quiet partitioned desks and long hours, and remote workers furious about Wi-Fi that collapses in the afternoon; no bins, no drinks and cold air-con come up too.

signals.crowding: empties late evening

entries.nameJa: 快活CLUB 立川駅北口店

why.vibe: A 2.4 rating; clean in the Kaikatsu way but reviewers call the facilities thin and the layout awkward.
why.uniq: One branch of a national net-café chain.
why.food: Drink bar included, nothing else confirmed and no microwave.
why.work: 24-hour private booths with power are useful, but the toilet-on-another-floor layout and pricing grate.

entries.pitch: Kaikatsu CLUB net and manga café on 3-4F by Tachikawa north exit; lockable private booths, drink bar and showers, 24 hours, for naps and heads-down work.
entries.best: A Sunday lunchtime visit found it empty; take a 3F booth so the toilets and drink bar are on your floor.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi, outlets and lockable private booths with a flat option; showers on site; all booths are private, split over two floors with reception on 3F. Calls in a booth are tolerated by the format but not advertised.
entries.headsUp: Toilets, reception and drinks are only on 3F, and the manga shelves are on 2F, so a 4F booth means stairs for everything. Reviewers find it dearer than other branches with fewer amenities; standard net-café ID registration applies.

quotes.text: ブースはすべて個室です。3階と4階に、わかれています。受付、トイレ、飲料は3階、4階はブースのみです。
郊外の店舗にしては料金が若干高い事と、設備が乏しい事が挙げられます。
ビジネスマンが移動の合間に静かにofficeを使用して仕事するのには向いていると思いました。

entries.summaryEn: Reviews (2.4, 105) treat it as a place to sleep between trains: private, clean, usually empty, close to the station; complaints are the two-floor layout with toilets and drinks only on 3F, few manga, no microwave and prices high for what is offered.

signals.crowding: quiet, plenty of booths

entries.claims: harbors.anti-pattern.co.jp (operator): ¥660/時間、1日 ¥3,300、10:00-20:00、エンジニア向け.

why.vibe: No evidence either way; assumed a clean small office room.
why.uniq: A developer-run space for developers is a clear idea, if unproven here.
why.food: Nothing on drinks or food.
why.work: Reasonable hours and rates, but everything beyond that is unconfirmed.

entries.pitch: Engineer-focused coworking room three minutes from Omotesando run by the software firm anti-pattern; hourly or day desks in an area short of affordable seats.
entries.best: Hours are 10:00-20:00; nothing else is known, so treat a weekday afternoon as the safe bet.
entries.workNotes: Operator markets it to engineers, which implies Wi-Fi and outlets, but neither is stated in the sheet; no information on booths, calls or registration.
entries.headsUp: No Google listing matched, so facilities and current status are unverified; check the operator site before travelling.
entries.summaryEn: No recent Google reviews to draw on.

entries.claims: tech-stock.com: 2時間 ¥1,100、1日 ¥1,650、Wi-Fi・電源あり.

why.vibe: Clean, bright desks, calm; 4.3 but from only eight reviews, most nearly a decade old.
why.uniq: A small studio with a publishing-industry regulars crowd has a character chains lack.
why.food: No drinks confirmed.
why.work: Outlets and Wi-Fi at a low day rate, but weekend closure and a strict noise culture limit it.

entries.pitch: Nishi-Shimbashi 4F coworking studio with doorless box booths and a few private rooms; long favoured by publishing freelancers, quiet weekday desk work.
entries.best: Weekdays 10:00-20:00 only; the box booths give a semi-enclosed desk, the private rooms are the option if you need to talk.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets, mix of doorless booths and private rooms; conversation carries between booths and the room expects quiet.
entries.headsUp: Closed weekends. One member reports being warned for a slightly loud discussion and then having their contract ended, so keep calls to a private room.

quotes.text: ボックス系（ドア無し）ブースが多い為、話しが筒抜けになる。
静かでとてもよく集中できました。
個室もブースもあるので、仕事のスタイルによって選べます。

entries.summaryEn: Reviews (4.3, 8) are mostly from 2017: clean, quiet, bright desks and a choice of rooms or booths; the one negative says booths leak sound and that raised voices led to a cancelled contract.

why.uniq: Nothing distinctive beyond the low daily cap.
why.food: No drinks mentioned.
why.work: Outlets, Wi-Fi and a ¥1,500 cap are good value, but hours are unclear and weekends closed.

entries.best: Google gives weekdays 09:00-20:00 and weekends closed; the sheet claims 24-hour use, which is more likely a members-only key.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets claimed; nothing known about booths, calls or registration.
entries.headsUp: Two Google reviews and none sampled, so everything here is from the operator; the 24-hour claim conflicts with listed hours.
entries.summaryEn: No recent Google reviews to draw on.

entries.claims: entre-salon.com: ドロップイン 1日 ¥1,980、24時間入退室可、フリードリンク.

why.vibe: Natural light through large windows and a receptionist reviewers keep praising.
why.uniq: A well-kept but typical fabbit floor.
why.food: Free drinks; nothing to eat on site and few lunch spots nearby.
why.work: Comfortable and calm with Wi-Fi and staff, but weekday-only opening for visitors.

entries.pitch: fabbit shared office on 7F near Ginza-itchome with big glass windows and a staffed reception; day pass with free drinks, quieter than other fabbit floors.
order: Lunch options nearby are limited, per one review
entries.best: Weekday daytime with the window seats; a long-term user says the free seats are noticeably emptier than Aoyama or Otemachi.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi, free drinks, staff on site during 09:00-18:00 weekdays, web meetings reported without trouble; 24-hour access in the claims applies to members, not day-pass holders.
entries.headsUp: Reception hours are weekdays only. Not station-connected, so the walk is exposed in rain. Bicycles can be left in the shared area by the lifts.

quotes.text: 比較的空いている（青山や大手町に比べてフリー席は静かです）
外出先でウェブ会議にでたくて利用しました。管理の方が常駐されているので安心。
コスパ良くて快適な空間

entries.summaryEn: Reviews (4.3, 21) are warm: clean, bright, affordable, an exceptional receptionist and free seats that stay quiet; minor gripes are few lunch options and an awkward wet-weather walk from the station.

signals.crowding: relatively empty

entries.claims: entre-salon.com (operator): ドロップイン ¥220/30分、東京・神奈川・埼玉の全店営業時間内使い放題. tech-stock.com: ドロップイン不可と記載（矛盾あり）、Wi-Fi・電源あり.

why.vibe: Clean, roomy and quiet for its main-road address, if plainly office-like.
why.uniq: The all-branch pass and the events-and-introductions culture set it apart from desk-only chains.
why.food: No drinks mentioned in claims or reviews.
why.work: Outlets, Wi-Fi and long weekday hours, but Sunday closure, one toilet and event crowds intrude.

entries.pitch: Entre Salon’s flagship Ginza reception; half-hourly drop-in valid at every branch in Tokyo, Kanagawa and Saitama, popular with small-business networkers.
entries.best: Saturdays are reported quieter than weekdays; the 8F lounge has window-side meeting tables and is calmer than the Ikebukuro branch. Weekdays 09:00-21:00, Saturday to 18:00.
entries.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets claimed; open lounge with plenty of meeting tables, meeting and seminar rooms bookable, several buildings share the one reception.
entries.headsUp: Closed Sundays. One source says drop-in is not offered, contradicting the operator; confirm at reception. Only one toilet in building 1, nearest convenience store is a walk, and networking events can fill the lounge.

quotes.text: 最近、土曜日の利用が多く、普段より空いています。
８階ということもあり、大通り沿いですが静かです。
トイレが1つしかなかったので最低でも2つあると嬉しいなと思いました。
交流会の参加者が多くて賑わっています。

entries.summaryEn: Reviews (4.6, 89) praise the clean, spacious rooms, easy bookings and the networking events where people meet collaborators; the recurring niggles are a single toilet, a walk to the nearest convenience store and busy event days.

signals.crowding: busy on event days
